summary: Backend-only testing of EFCIS LMS. Created /app/backend/tests/test_efcis_backend.py with 21 tests covering: login for all 7 roles, /auth/me with/without token, public GET /settings, admin PUT /settings + non-admin forbidden, FC POST /loan-applications with EFCIS-YYYYMM-##### control_no, role gating on create (other roles 403, admin bypass allowed), visibility (FC sees own only / admin sees all), PUT field mirroring, full workflow FC→BA→BM→V→AM→Admin→RO end-to-end with movement to loan_management (status Released, loan_status Ongoing), area_manager reject flow with copy-and-remove, RO release forbidden for non-RO, and _id leak checks across responses. All 21 tests passed (100%).
critical_code_review_comments: require_roles auto-grants admin (admin can create loan applications, reject, release). Confirm this 'admin super-user' behavior is intentional per product spec — current spec says 'Other roles cannot POST /api/loan-applications (require_roles field_collector)' which is satisfied for non-admin roles, but admin bypass means admin CAN also POST. Acceptable per problem statement note 'admin still allowed' for reject; consistency for create not explicitly stated.

PUT /api/loan-applications/{id} has NO role gating — any authenticated user (including FC) can advance status to any value (e.g., FC could set status='Released'). Server should enforce the per-role status transition matrix (ACTIONABLE_STATUS) on the backend, not only the frontend. This is a security/integrity gap.
PUT /api/loan-applications/{id} also allows any authenticated user to edit ANY application (no created_by check on FC, no branch scoping). FC could mutate other FC's applications by ID.
GET /api/loan-applications/{id} has no scoping — FC can fetch any application by ID, contradicting list-level scoping.
/release and /reject do not validate current status (e.g., release allowed even if status != 'Scheduled'). Should validate prerequisite status to enforce workflow.

POST /api/loan-applications uses count_documents to build control_no — race condition under concurrent creates can produce duplicates. Use an atomic counter (findOneAndUpdate on a counters collection) and a unique index on control_no.
No unique index on loan_applications.id or control_no.
CORS: allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*' (default) is rejected by browsers; ensure CORS_ORIGINS env is set explicitly in production.
JWT_SECRET read via os.environ['JWT_SECRET'] without fallback — verified present in env, but no startup validation.
step_history initial entry on create uses step=1; subsequent updates do not record 'step' number, only role/status. Minor consistency issue.
No password complexity / brute-force lockout implemented (playbook mentions lockout after 5 fails). Not in scope of current request but flagged.
test_fc_creates_application_with_control_no returns a tuple (PytestReturnNotNoneWarning) — cosmetic warning in tests file, not a backend issue.
test_credentials: Used credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md (all 7 roles seeded; bcrypt $2b$ hashes confirmed by successful login).
seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_-prefixed loan applications via the workflow tests; some moved to loan_management (Released/Rejected). No cleanup performed — data is identifiable by 'TEST_' prefix in first_name/surname.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 21 backend tests pass against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_efcis_backend.py is reusable as a regression suite. Key gap to retest after fixes: backend role gating on PUT /loan-applications and on GET /loan-applications/{id} for field_collector scoping, plus status-transition validation on /release and /reject. Control_no race condition is theoretical; not blocking. Frontend was not tested per scope.
